'''Dany Leviatan''' ({{Langx|he|דני לויתן}}; born 21 February 1942) is an Israeli mathematician and former [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of [[Tel Aviv University]].

==Biography==
Dany Leviatan completed his B.Sc. and M.Sc. at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. A participant in the [[Atuda|Academic Atuda]] program, Leviatan served as a mathematician in the [[Israel Air Force]] while working on his doctorate at the Hebrew University, which he completed in 1966.

==Academic career==
He worked as visiting professor at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] from 1967 to 1970 through the [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholarship Program]], and became [[associate professor]] at [[Tel Aviv University]] in 1972. Leviatan served as head of the university's Department of Mathematics from 1972 to 1974, and dean of the Faculty of Exact Sciences from 1976 to 1980. He became head of the recently established School of Mathematics in 1982.<ref name=iljaen>{{cite web|url=http://www.ujaen.es/revista/jja/jca/2011/leviatan.php|date=2011|website=II Jaen Conference on Approximation Theory|title=About Dany Leviatan|access-date=22 February 2019}}</ref>

Leviatan was appointed [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of Tel Aviv University on 16 August 2005, a position he kept until 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://english.tau.ac.il/past_leadership|title=Past Leadership of Tel Aviv University|website=Tel Aviv University|access-date=2 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.com/1.5071437|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622041808/https://www.haaretz.com/1.5071437|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 22, 2018|title=Rector Bars Law Clinic From Acting Against Other Schools|newspaper=[[Haaretz]]|date=10 December 2008|first=Ruth|last=Sinai|access-date=22 February 2019}}</ref> He briefly served as acting president of the university following the resignation of [[Zvi Galil]] in July 2009.
